Start working on Linear ticket eng-2228 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2228` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2228`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's premise is wrong, and ENG-2227 already confirmed it on the Roam side.** There is no app-side geo-link code to reuse — in `apps/obsidian` the entire link feature (the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog`, the corner icon) is stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So this is a **schema change, not UI wiring**. Once `text` props carry `url`, the context-menu item and dialog light up for free — `CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and there is no `actions` override anywhere in the app.

This plan mirrors the ENG-2227 Roam implementation (written, statically verified, not yet merged) so the two apps stay consistent. Roam's settled decisions carry over; the deltas are called out below.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration (it's `T.jsonValue`), but it would require hand-rolling the menu item and dialog — exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids.
- **A migration is mandatory, not optional.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` doesn't work: the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent, so old text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Without the migration, `migrateStoreSnapshot` reports *success* and does nothing, then validation throws `At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined`.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`). An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both `TextShapeUtil` and a subclass throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (confirmed absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Obsidian-specific deltas

| | Roam | Obsidian |
|---|---|---|
| Registration sites | 4 | **2** — `utils/tldraw.ts:55` and `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109` |
| Migration home | appended v6 to `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` | **new sequence at v1** (see below) |
| Sync worker | needed `"text"` added to `shapeType` params | **N/A** — file-based; cross-tab merge goes through `store.schema.migrateStoreSnapshot`, which applies the retroactive migration |
| Test infra | vitest exists | **none — must be stood up** |

The migration goes in a **new** sequence `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` starting at version 1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations`. Roam appended because its sequence is generically named; Obsidian's existing one is `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.discourse-node`, and a text-shape migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1, so a fresh sequence is legal. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what makes it backfill files that predate it.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`:

```tsx
const textShapeWithLinkProps = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl };

export class TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil {
  static override props = textShapeWithLinkProps;

  override getDefaultProps(): TextShapeWithLinkProps {
    return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" };
  }

  override component(shape: TLTextShape): ReturnType<TextShapeUtil["component"]> {
    const url = getTextShapeUrl(shape);
    return (<>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton url={url} .../>}</>) as ...;
  }
}
```

Three things that are load-bearing:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone does not add a default — the base returns an object literal, so every `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **`super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite would silently drop Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched and keeps sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill has to be a separate store-level sequence.

Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than through `useValue`; mirror it for consistency (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `src/components/canvas/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers, ported verbatim from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts`: `isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`. These exist so the migration logic is unit-testable without an editor or the Obsidian API.

### 3. `src/components/canvas/shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

### 4. `src/components/canvas/shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils: TLAnyShapeUtilConstructor[] =
  defaultShapeUtils.map((util) => (util === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : util));
```

Then `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68` (`migrations: [discourseNodeMigrations, textLinkMigrations]`).

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` uses one for the *schema*, the `Editor` uses the other for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws on validation; update only the store and links persist but never render. That silent divergence is the reason for the shared module, same as Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — it only runs with zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load regardless.

### 5. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` for `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"` to devDependencies. Per [memory: avoid `pnpm add` here], edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`.
- No turbo.json change: `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, and root `ci:validate` picks it up.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed — the test imports only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless in plain node; no jsdom.)
- `vitest` must be a real devDep because `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts the test files under `check-types`.

`src/components/canvas/utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite: the backfill is idempotent and never overwrites a user value, non-text records are untouched, a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails, and — via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema — an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot`. That last pair is the highest-value test: the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw and rendering a blank canvas.

## Known tradeoffs to surface in the PR

- **`obsidian://` page links will not work.** `T.linkUrl` accepts only `http:`/`https:`/`mailto:` (`@tldraw/validate` `validLinkProtocols`), and tldraw's `EditLinkDialog` rejects other protocols on input before the schema ever sees them. So "link to a page" — which the ticket calls the primary expected target — isn't reachable through this path. This *is* exact geo parity and matches "no new link format"; Roam shipped the same. Flag it and suggest a follow-up ticket rather than forking the dialog.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early, so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.
- **Convert To drops the url.** `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` only reads `props.richText`. Correct (text→node conversion is out of scope), but say so in the PR so it isn't read as a regression.
- Worth a Linear comment to Michael that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise, so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction. Same note applies to ENG-2227.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`. Then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build actually contains the change. Lint: check for new *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian** (the part static checks can't cover — ENG-2227 is still blocked on exactly this):
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** is present. Select two shapes, or lock the shape → absent.
2. Set `https://example.com` → corner icon appears; click → opens; reopen dialog → pre-filled; **Clear** → icon gone.
3. **The icon's stacking is the most likely thing to be wrong.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1` — so for a text shape the label may cover the icon and swallow the click, in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and the `--layer-text-editor` overlay still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add the rule pre-emptively.
4. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
5. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; then read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
6. **Backfill:** open a canvas file created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
7. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## Files

**Modified** — `src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts` (lines 56, 68), `src/components/canvas/TldrawViewComponent.tsx` (line 109), `apps/obsidian/package.json`.

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side.
```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side. There is no app-side geo-link code in `apps/obsidian` — the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog` and the corner icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

**Scope decision (2026-09-14):** the ticket names page links as the primary target, so this ships `obsidian://open?vault=…&file=…` support alongside web URLs. That goes beyond strict geo parity and beyond what ENG-2227 shipped for Roam — deliberately. `obsidian://` is already this canvas's link currency: `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) and `buildObsidianUrl` (`wikilinkDragHandler.ts:14`) exist, and dropping such a URL on the canvas already creates a discourse node shape.

*Known limitation to state in the PR:* an `obsidian://` URL inside our fenced JSON block is invisible to Obsidian's link machinery — no backlinks, no graph view, and it breaks if the vault or page is renamed. The plugin's own richer pattern for this (a real `[[wikilink]]` block plus a block-ref id in `props.src`, `assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. Worth a follow-up ticket; not this one.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration but would require hand-rolling the menu item.
- **A migration is mandatory.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` *does* validate an absent key (`optional()` returns early on `undefined`, `validation.mjs:594-598`) — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is missing, so pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Optional only changes what a migration *miss* looks like.
- **`url` is required, not optional** (confirmed 2026-09-14): geo parity, and a migration miss then fails loudly rather than silently hiding the feature. Optional wouldn't help the downgrade case anyway — an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` regardless, since its own validator config has no such key.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`) — independent of the required/optional choice. An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Implementation

### 1. `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, with the validator and click handling widened:

```tsx
static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: textLinkUrl };
override getDefaultProps() { return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" }; }
override component(shape) { return <>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton .../>}</>; }
```

Load-bearing details:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone gives no default — the base returns an object literal, so `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **Call `super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite silently drops Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched at sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill must be a separate store-level sequence.
- Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than via `useValue`; mirror it (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers ported from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (`isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`), plus the widened validator:

```ts
const ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS = ["http:", "https:", "mailto:", "obsidian:"];
export const textLinkUrl = T.string.check(validateTextLinkUrl);
```

**This allowlist is a security boundary, not a formality** — the affordance renders `<a href={url}>`, so accepting arbitrary protocols would make `javascript:` an XSS vector. Enumerate; never fall through to "anything that parses".

Keeping these helpers free of `obsidian` imports is what makes them unit-testable without mocks.

### 3. `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

A **new** sequence starting at v1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations` — Roam appended because its sequence is generically named, whereas Obsidian's is `…obsidian.discourse-node` and a text migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what backfills files predating it.

### 4. `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils = defaultShapeUtils.map((u) =>
  u === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : u);
```

Swap `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68`.

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` for the *schema*, the `Editor` for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws; update only the store and links persist but never render. Hence the shared module, as in Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load anyway.

### 5. `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (new) + an `edit-link` action override

tldraw's dialog gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`), so it rejects `obsidian://` *before* the schema sees it. Widening the validator alone accomplishes nothing — the dialog must be forked.

`EditLinkDialog` itself is not exported, but every primitive it uses is (`TldrawUiDialogBody/Header/Footer/Title/CloseButton`, `TldrawUiInput`, `TldrawUiButton`, `TldrawUiButtonLabel`), so the fork is a faithful, visually identical copy with `validateUrl` swapped.

Swap it in via the supported `TLUiOverrides.actions` hook (`index.d.mts:3747`), extending the existing `overrides` object at `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:466` (currently `tools` only). Replace only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` — `helpers.addDialog({ component: TextLinkDialog })`, preceded by `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint("edit-link")` as the stock action does (`actions.tsx:153-160`). Label, icon, placement and the eligibility gate all stay stock.

**The trap:** this override is global, so the forked dialog also serves *geo* shapes — whose `url` prop is still stock `T.linkUrl`. Letting an `obsidian://` URL through for a geo shape would throw at `editor.updateShapes`. The dialog must therefore pick its validator from the selected shape's type (wide for `text`, stock `T.linkUrl` otherwise). Cover this with a test; it is the most likely silent regression in the change.

### 6. Click handling in the vendored button

Branch on protocol. Web/mailto → plain `<a href target="_blank">`, exactly as geo. `obsidian:` → `preventDefault`, then `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) → resolve to a `TFile` → `openFileInSidebar` (`openFileUtils.ts:68`). Handling it in-app avoids an OS protocol round trip that would defocus and re-enter Obsidian.

`resolveObsidianUrlToFile` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:56`) already does the vault-name check and the `.md` suffix retry — export it rather than writing a second copy. Show a `Notice` when the target is another vault or missing (per house style, `Notice`, not `console.*`).

### 7. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).

- `vitest` must be a real devDep: `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts test files under `check-types`.

`utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite plus the new validator cases:
- backfill is idempotent, never overwrites a user value, leaves non-text records alone;
- a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails;

  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.

---
name: reference-tldraw-store-put-no-listener
description: "tldraw store.listen() does not fire for a programmatic store.put(), so CDP-driven canvas edits never trigger the autosave — drive real input events instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

A raw `store.put()` on the Obsidian canvas's `TLStore` (reachable over CDP as
`app.workspace.getLeavesOfType("tldraw-dg-preview")[0].view.store`) updates the store and
re-renders the shape, but **fires no `store.listen()` callbacks** — verified by registering a
listener with the same `{ source: "user", scope: "document" }` options the plugin uses and
counting 0 calls. The plugin's autosave hangs off that listener, so programmatic puts never
reach the markdown file and look like a persistence bug in whatever you just built.

Diagnose it by checking the *store* and the *file* separately over time: shape present in
store + absent from file, indefinitely, means the listener never fired — not that saving is broken.

Drive real input instead (`Input.dispatchMouseEvent` / `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` /
`Input.insertText`): select the tool, click to place, type, Escape. That exercises the editor,
flushes the reactor, and the 500 ms `DEFAULT_SAVE_DELAY` debounce then writes the file. Real
input is also the only way to test shape *creation*, which is where `getDefaultProps` bugs
surface.

Related gotchas found the same way:
- `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` rejects `text: undefined` — omit the key entirely on `keyUp` and for
  non-printable keys like Escape, or CDP returns `Invalid 'text' parameter`.
- Counting `.tl-shape` elements immediately after a store load reads 0 because React has not
  painted yet. Poll for the count instead of asserting once, or you will misread viewport
  culling / paint timing as a blank canvas.
- `document.elementFromPoint` at a shape's hyperlink icon returns `.tl-canvas`, not the anchor —
  for geo shapes too. tldraw hit-tests through its own canvas layer, so this is not evidence of a
  z-index bug. Always measure a stock shape type as a control before believing a rendering regression.

## What it does

Text shapes gained a `url` prop, which is all tldraw's duck-typed gate (`'url' in shape.props`) needs — the **Edit link** item, its icon and placement come from stock tldraw untouched. Because you chose page-link support, the validator is widened past tldraw's `T.linkUrl` to an explicit allowlist (`http`/`https`/`mailto`/`obsidian`), and the dialog is forked, since tldraw's own rejects non-web protocols on input before the schema ever sees them.

**New:** `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `baseShapeUtils.ts`, `textLinkMigrations.ts`, `utils/textShapeLink.ts`, `TextLinkDialog.tsx`, tests, `vitest.config.mts`.
**Modified:** the two shape-util registration sites, the `overrides` block, `externalContentHandlers.ts` (export the resolver), `styles.css`, `package.json`.

## Verified in Obsidian, not just statically

`ci:validate` green (6 tasks, 0 cached); types, lint, build clean; 10 new unit tests. Then driven over CDP against testVault:

- **Edit link** appears under Edit ▸ for a text shape
- The forked dialog accepts an `obsidian://` URL and enables Save — stock tldraw would have blocked it
- Clicking the icon opens the target page in the sidebar
- A text shape created through the real toolbar gets `url: ""` — without the `getDefaultProps` override every text-shape creation would have thrown

- A genuine pre-change file (url stripped, sequence removed) loads, backfills both text shapes to `url: ""`, and renders — no blank canvas
- `javascript:` is rejected by the allowlist, which matters because the affordance is an `<a href>`

Two things I flagged in the plan turned out not to be real. The z-index concern didn't materialize — a geo shape measures **identically**, so that's tldraw's hit-testing, not a text-specific regression. And an early "nothing persists" result was my harness, not the code: tldraw's `store.listen` doesn't fire for a programmatic `store.put`, so autosave never ran; real input events save fine. I've saved that one to memory.

## Worth knowing before the PR

- **`obsidian://` links are invisible to Obsidian's link graph** — no backlinks, and they break on vault or page rename. The plugin's own `[[wikilink]]` + block-ref pattern (`assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. I'd open a follow-up.

> *Revisit if:* we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback.

That condition has now fired, and Michael found it from the other direction.

**And one of my two reasons was wrong.** I said meta forces hand-rolling "the menu item and dialog". The dialog is needed either way — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`, so the 214-line fork exists because of page-link support, not because of props-vs-meta. The real marginal cost of meta is only the menu item plus a gate hook, ~40 lines. So the argument I leaned on was roughly half as strong as I stated.

## What the research says now

Net code is **~60-70 lines lighter** under meta, not the big simplification Michael hopes for — a custom shape util is required either way, because the util is what renders the icon. On his actual framing, "reuses more of tldraw", meta is **backwards**: it forfeits all three stock menu entries.

But the decisive trade isn't line count, it's compatibility:

| | `props.url` (current) | `meta.url` |
|---|---|---|
| Old build opens a new file | `Unexpected property: url` → **blank canvas** | loads fine, ignores the link, **round-trips it intact on save** |
| Migration + schema-fallback plumbing | ~57 lines | **gone** — which also deletes the code Michael called "suspicious" |
| URL validation | enforced at load by the schema | only on write — needs a **render-time guard**, or `javascript:` in a hand-edited file reaches `<a href>` |

Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so the blank-canvas mode is the serious one. There's also direct precedent: `relationInstanceId` already lives in `shape.meta` in this plugin.

Two further findings worth knowing before you decide:

- **A patch is viable and cheap for the *validator*.** Patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` (2 files) makes `obsidian://` work for text *and* geo consistently, and fixes the stock dialog for free — which would let us delete our dialog fork. Michael's remembered embed-hostname patch is real but was deleted by the very next tldraw upgrade, so it survived exactly one version.
- **Click behaviour is genuinely inconsistent today**, and he's right to flag it. Discourse nodes: cmd+click → new tab, shift+click → sidebar. Our text link: cmd+click → **sidebar**. Same modifier, different destination.

My recommendation is to switch to `meta.url` — it answers his question, deletes the schema work he objected to, and fixes the rollback hazard — combined with the validator patch so the dialog fork goes too.
